comments.body: The claim that the C code never asks for more than 24 bits has no C source citation. STYLE.md requires citations for claims about the vendored C source. Please cite the relevant call sites that establish this bound, or remove the parenthetical claim.

These test helper declarations (`bytes`, `readAll`, `values`, etc.) are at the root namespace. STYLE.md requires declarations to live in the namespace named after their module, with exceptions only for the listed oracle API modules. Please put the helpers in `Bzip2.Test.BitIO` (the guards can be in that namespace too).

last.summary: The bit reader and writer match the checked upstream bit order and byte flushing, and the task check passes. I checked `decompress.c:43-65` (MSB extraction and input exhaustion), `decompress.c:89-95` (Huffman width limit), `compress.c:58-78` (byte flushing and bit placement), `compress.c:650` (24-bit origPtr), and `compress.c:46-55` (final byte); the task's `Error.eof` choice for a short read is implemented. Two STYLE.md issues remain below.
